stem:
Bhavna notes visible changes in classmates over a year: increased height, broader shoulders in some, a deeper voice in one friend, and a few pimples.

Which claim about these changes is correct?

options.text: These can be normal adolescent changes, and not every person shows the same changes in the same way.
Every adolescent must show all of these changes, in the same order, at the same time.
These changes mean adolescence is unrelated to growing from childhood toward adulthood.
Pimples alone prove that a person is not an adolescent.

teacher.key_rationale: Increased height, broader shoulders, voice change, and pimples can be normal adolescent changes, and they are not identical for every person.
